title: Conditional assignment dominates expected payoff
statement: Let $D$ be a finite nonempty set, let $n\geq 0$, and assign a probability mass function $p_i$ on $D$ to each coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For every payoff function $F:D^n\to\mathbb{R}$, its expectation under independent coordinate sampling is at most its value at the assignment chosen by successively maximizing the conditional expected payoff of the remaining coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nonempty set of coordinate values
A probability mass function on the value set for each coordinate
